text:
incident-bot: :warning: Alert — Elevated 5xx rate and p50 latency in eu-central-1 for Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Metric spike looks correlated with LogProviderX ingest API 429s. Auto-runbook triggered: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/logs-ingest-degradation

sre-oncall: I'm on it. paging oncall-sre list now. seeing 503s in the edge-proxy logs too.

mia: Confirmed. 5xxs started ~12:02 UTC, error rate ~2.5% for hosted, Dedicated pool p95 latency + 300ms.

raj: Correlates with increased error counts from our obs-proxy to LogProviderX. Provider returning 429s for bulk upload.

kelsey: Any customer-facing impact? CS starting a watch.

mia: Early impact: real-time ingestion customers (logs and events) see backpressure which touches control-plane paths for hosted token refresh + some request fanout. A subset of requests for embeddings/time-series hit 503s.

support-bot: Open support thread created: #SUP-4621, flagged high priority, initial AffectedCustomers: 3 (one enterprise, two scale-ups).

raj: Quick mitigation steps I'm going to try: 1) enable local buffering on obs-proxy, 2) reduce batch sizes to avoid provider rate limits, 3) add short-term fallback for log writes to S3 archive.

mia: Also scaling Dedicated EU pools by +2 instances to absorb retry fanout. Kicking off now.

sre-oncall: Execute the fallback routing I posted in runbook. Command to flip routing (internal-only):
```bash
# promote fallback route for eu-central-1 logs write
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-central-1 --route fallback-logs-archive --reason "LogProviderX 429 surge"
```

ops-bot: Route change recorded: fallback-logs-archive applied by sre-oncall at 12:14 UTC.

kelsey: Noted. CS updating impacted customers with a brief: "We are routing log ingest to archival fallback to reduce errors; no data loss expected."

mia: After routing flip, error rate dropped from 2.5% -> 0.6% for hosted API 5xx in eu-central-1. Latency improved but still elevated.

raj: Observability gap: LogProviderX's status page shows partial rate-limiting in eu-central region. Their support ticket #LPX-917 in progress.

sre-oncall: We're keeping the channel for live mitigation. On-call handoff at 12:45 UTC to raj for overnight monitoring. I'll annotate the incident timeline.

mia: Running a targeted canary to un-route 10% traffic back in 15m to validate stability.

support-bot: Notifying customers: email dispatched to affected accounts at 12:21 UTC.

raj: Canary results at 12:35 — canary 10% showed stable 5xx ~0.8% (within baseline). Rolling 50% in 5m.

kelsey: Customers acknowledging the update. One asked about SLA credits; legal + finance pinged.

mia: Plan: keep fallback routing for logs ingestion for 24 hours, continue scaling Dedicated pools if needed, and monitor LogProviderX ticket. Postmortem owner: mia. ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

sre-oncall: Handing off to raj now. If degraded again, page @sre-oncall immediately. Closing short-lived alert but keeping incident open.

raj: taking over — monitoring dashboards, tied to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/logs-ingest-degradation. Will update every 30m or on change.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to 'mitigated' (partial): mitigation applied, fallback routing active, oncall: raj.

kelsey: Recording customer impact summary for postmortem: ~2.5% peak request 5xx (hosted), ~3 customers with visible errors, no confirmed data loss due to archival fallback.

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-4621 updated with mitigation notes and customer emails.

mia: Adding a short-term observability action: add alert threshold for provider-429s on obs-proxy to warn at 5/min per region.

sre-oncall: Agreed. Also add retry-smoothing to reduce simultaneous retries after provider rate-limit signals.

raj: Logging final checkpoint before handoff end at 12:54 UTC — overall posture stable, watch on LogProviderX ticket. If they recover, we'll gradually undo fallback and monitor for regressions.

kelsey: Thanks all. I'll coordinate customer comms and postmortem stakeholders. :pray:
